source.title: MinimalRNN: Toward More Interpretable and Trainable Recurrent Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Reports recurrent-network training and Jacobian results on a production recommendation task, a setting outside the claim versions’ classification benchmarks. It does not measure CIFAR training classification error or directly test any listed version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on recommendation performance and Jacobian conditioning, not training classification error. It does not compare initializations; unitary initialization is held fixed. Figure 4 and Figure 5 values are shown as plots, so only the paper’s textual descriptions are recorded. Cited findings from other work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses unitary initialization and Jacobian conditioning to motivate and evaluate recurrent architectures. It holds initialization fixed and compares architectures on recommendation performance and Jacobian spectra; these results do not test any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: MinimalRNN matches the tested gated models' recommendation performance, trains faster, and maintains better-conditioned Jacobians. Longer-range dependency capture is suggested by those Jacobians rather than directly demonstrated by a separate task measure; applicability beyond this task remains open.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies recurrent architectures on production recommendation and Jacobian conditioning, rather than training classification error on image benchmarks. All recurrent-network weights are initialized to be unitary; no initialization comparison is reported.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported Jacobian behavior differs by recurrent architecture and by k; Vanilla RNN fails early, GRU Jacobians stretch and shrink, and CFN Jacobians shrink during learning, while MinimalRNN Jacobians remain relatively well-conditioned.

fits_no_version.finding: Vanilla RNN failed early from gradient explosion in both displayed runs. GRU, CFN, and MinimalRNN reached test MAP@20 near 0.15; training took 46, 36, and 30 hours respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Recurrent architecture affects training failure and runtime on this production recommendation task despite similar final recommendation performance among the gated models.

fits_no_version.finding: With unitary initialization held fixed, recurrent architectures differed in Jacobian conditioning across sequence distances and during training; MinimalRNN remained relatively well-conditioned.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Recurrent architecture affects input-output Jacobian conditioning under unitary initialization.

record.peer_reviewed: Interpretable ML Symposium, 31st Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2017)
record.problems: The evidence concerns one production recommendation task, not classification benchmarks. The main Jacobian comparisons are presented in figures and described qualitatively; the text gives no error bars or statistical uncertainty. All recurrent-network weights use unitary initialization, so initialization effects are not compared.

untested.parts: All parts: convolutional-network training classification error on CIFAR, including random labels and recipe or size effects.
All parts: teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious minima, and excess student width.
All parts: depth degradation, identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization and normalization exceptions.
All parts: initialization comparisons, activation matching, learning speed, trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian weights or convolution kernels.
All parts: learning-rate thresholds, curvature dynamics, loss recovery, edge of stability, and divergence.
All parts: batch normalization's effects on speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training.

record.verdict_notes: A new application setting alone does not warrant T3 when no listed version is tested. Unitary initialization is a shared experimental choice, so neither successful training nor failure isolates its effect.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR classification training error, random or corrupted labels, and effects of size, early stopping, or regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth effects in plain versus residual convolutional networks, including shortcuts and normalization.
Comparisons of initialization schemes, activation-matched initialization, depth, and orthogonal convolutional kernels.
Learning rates around stability limits, curvature, loss recovery, and divergence.
Batch normalization’s effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup residual training.

rows.subject: Vanilla RNN
rows.operation_detail: Trained as the recurrent component of the production recommender; all recurrent-network weights initialized to be unitary.
rows.value: failed during early stage of the learning due to gradient explosion
rows.note: The paper reports an explicit training failure; it does not report classification error.
rows.check: Early training failure is reported correctly, but the measure should be training failure from gradient explosion, not test MAP@20. This recurrent-network result does not establish absence of any listed effect.

rows.subject: GRU
rows.operation_detail: Trained as the recurrent component of the production recommender; all recurrent-network weights initialized to be unitary.
rows.note: Reported as performing rather similarly to CFN and MinimalRNN.
rows.check: Test MAP@20 measures recommendation performance, not any listed effect.

rows.subject: CFN
rows.operation_detail: Trained as the recurrent component of the production recommender; all recurrent-network weights initialized to be unitary.
rows.note: Reported as performing rather similarly to GRU and MinimalRNN.
rows.check: Test MAP@20 measures recommendation performance, not any listed effect.

rows.subject: MinimalRNN
rows.operation_detail: Trained as the recurrent component of the production recommender; all recurrent-network weights initialized to be unitary.
rows.note: Reported as performing rather similarly to GRU and CFN.
rows.check: This is the proposed architecture's test recommendation performance, not a test of any listed effect.

rows.subject: MinimalRNN
rows.operation_detail: Training time for the production recommender.
rows.note: The authors attribute the shorter training time to the simpler update.
rows.check: The durations are correct, but the comparison changes recurrent architecture rather than initialization or batch normalization. It does not measure the speed effect in V4 or V6.

rows.subject: Vanilla RNN

conditions.value: weight matrices random initialized to be unitary

rows.measure: distribution of input-output Jacobian singular values
rows.value: singular values quickly vanish towards zero as k increases
rows.note: Qualitative description of the plotted result.
rows.check: Jacobian spectra across sequence distances under one initialization do not test initialization-dependent learning speed or trainable depth.

rows.subject: GRU
rows.operation_detail: Measured Jacobian singular-value distributions during learning.
rows.measure: distribution of input-output Jacobian singular values
rows.value: singular values of the Jacobian matrix in GRU grows rapidly in some iterations
rows.note: The authors say this suggests back-propagation error could be stretching over those directions.
rows.check: Jacobian singular-value growth is neither loss curvature nor a learning-rate stability threshold, and initialization is not compared.

rows.measure: distribution of input-output Jacobian singular values

rows.note: Qualitative description of the plotted result.
rows.check: Shrinking recurrent Jacobian singular values during training do not measure any listed version's effect.

rows.subject: MinimalRNN
rows.operation_detail: Measured Jacobian singular-value distributions during learning.
rows.measure: distribution of input-output Jacobian singular values
rows.value: Jacobians of MinimalRNN are relatively well-conditioned throughout the learning
rows.note: The authors state similar trends for different values of k, k > 10.
rows.check: Figure 5 uses k=10 and k=25; the text additionally reports similar trends for k>10. The condition conflates these. Conditioning remains a proxy rather than a test of initialization-dependent speed or depth.
